name: CDC Epidemic Trends and Rt
description:
An archive of estimated trend categories, probabilities of epidemic growth, and Rt, updated weekly for COVID-19 and flu. Estimates are based on emergency department visits reported to the National Syndromic Surveillance Program (NSSP), and generated using a model that includes nowcasting to adjust for incomplete reports on the most recent dates. See the visuals supported by these data, and more information about the data, models and methods at https://www.cdc.gov/cfa-modeling-and-forecasting/rt-estimates/index.html, and https://www.cdc.gov/respiratory-viruses/data/activity-levels.html.

For a semi-technical overview of the modeling methods used to generate these estimates see https://www.cdc.gov/cfa-behind-the-model/php/data-research/rt-estimates/index.html.

Note: On June 1, 2026 the modeling methods used to generate these estimates changed.

For `as_of` dates prior to 2026-06-01, estimates were generated using a semi-mechanistic Bayesian model run using the R package EpiNow2. Models were run independently in each state. Source code is available at https://github.com/CDCgov/cfa-epinow2-pipeline.

For `as_of` dates after 2026-06-01, estimates were generated using a hierarchical generalized additive model (HGAM) in which data were spatially partially pooled. Methods details are available at https://www.cdc.gov/cfa-behind-the-model/php/data-research/rt-estimates/index.html

columns.name: disease
columns.description: Disease for which Rt was estimated (e.g. COVID-19 or influenza)

columns.name: state
columns.description: Name of the state for which Rt was estimated, or "United States" for the national estimate

columns.name: date
columns.description: Date for which Rt was estimated

columns.name: median
columns.description: Median estimate of Rt for the disease, state, and date

columns.name: lower
columns.description: Lower bound of the credible interval of Rt for the disease, state, and date

columns.name: upper
columns.description: Upper bound of the credible interval of Rt for the disease, state, and date

columns.name: interval_width
columns.description: Width of the credible interval. (Interpretation: there is a 95% posterior probability that the true Rt value falls within the 95% credible interval, and so on for other interval widths)

columns.name: p_growing
columns.description: Estimated probability that Rt is above one (defined as the fraction of the credible interval that falls above one)

columns.name: category
columns.description: Reported epidemic trend category for the disease, state, and model run (as_of date), as published in the map visuals linked in the dataset description

Data Quality.Suggested Citation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Center for Forecasting and Outbreak Analytics, Epidemic Trend based on Rt [date]

Common Core.Contact Name: Center for Forecasting and Outbreak Analytics

metadata.rowLabel: Each row is an estimate of the epidemic trend, probability of epidemic growth, and Rt for a specific location, disease, date, and model run. The trend category and probability of growth are specific to the final date in the the model run (as_of date), and the Rt estimates are specific to each date in the run.
